newsitem.title: USA: Army transfers commander of Aberdeen training school.
newsitem.headline: Army transfers commander of Aberdeen training school.

text.p: The U.S. Army announced on Wednesday it was transferring the commander of its scandal- plagued Aberdeen Proving Ground training school, but denied the move had anything to do with a major sexual harassment scandal at Aberdeen.

Maj. Gen. Robert Shadley, who has headed the Ordnance Center and School at the big Aberdeen base in Maryland for two years, will be reassigned to another job at the headquarters of U.S. Army Forces Command at Fort McPherson, Ga., where he will become director of logistics.

But Lt. Col. Bill Harkey, an Army spokesman at the Pentagon, said the move of Shadley, 56, was routine after two years in a post and had nothing to do with charges and convictions of sexual harassment and rape of female recruits by male drill sergeants at Aberdeen. The scandal has also erupted at other training bases.

"It has nothing to do with Longhauser or the issues at Aberdeen. This is just a normal rotation," Harkey told Reuters. The service on Tuesday also announced the retirement from the Army of the overall commander of the Aberdeen base, Maj. Gen. John Longhouser, who admitted to an adulterous affair years ago.
The Army and other U.S. military services have been hit hard recently by cases of sexual harassment and marital cheating which have seen the removal or resignation of a number of senior officers.

The Pentagon has made no determination to date on whether lack of supervision by military and civilian leaders created a lax atmosphere for the problems at Aberdeen, where 12 trainers at the Ordnance Center and School have been charged with preying on female trainees.
